references.text: The same introductory formula where the Lord speaks to Moses, a common formula for introducing divine commands in the books of Moses.
An identical introductory formula at the beginning of Leviticus, where the Lord calls out to Moses and speaks to him.
The same formula is used to introduce the laws concerning sin offerings, showing the repeated pattern of divine revelation to Moses.
Introduces the chapter on clean and unclean animals, which thematically connects with the purity laws in chapter 12.
The Lord speaks to Moses, the same revelation formula used consistently throughout Numbers.
Another occurrence of the standardized formula for divine speech to Moses regarding purity laws.
